name: OakDoorDuel
source:
A large door, made from oak wood with beautiful and creative designs of lions, dragons and knights engraved on the door was creaked open. Clanks of metal could be heard, echoing throughout the large hallways bouncing off the granite falls and off the expansive roof. What laid behind the door a larger room. With a marble floor, high decretive walls and a window that looked out into the lush meadow with willow trees, oak trees, and even ash with a pond visible. A grand patio craved from granite had two pathways of stairs wrapping around a hedge that lead into the beautiful artificial sight of nature. 
 
 Inside the room, the hollow clanking could be traced to two individuals. Their fencing swords going back and forth, from offensive strikes to defensive blocks. 
 
 Clank. Clank. Clink. 
 
 `` Oof'' came from the mouth of an individual. His opponent had deflecting his strike and charged his shoulder into him. Stunning him, but not for long as he saw the metal bulb coming at him and shifted his body to the side parallel to the wall and swipe to deflect the strike. He leaped backward and took off his mask. 
 
 `` You cheater'' he bellowed his voice full of anger from an aged faced 
 
 `` All is fair in love and war'' a higher pitch voice had said from the mask. 
 
 He knew he was smiling underneath the mask that's how it was with common folk and his friend was no exception. 
 
 `` I can return the favor you know'' he shouted at him, he could n't keep his anger from showing as much as he tried not to give his friend the satisfaction of seeing him angered. 
 
 His friend resumed position. His hand, his arm behind him outstretched, crouched and his sword pointing toward him 
 
 `` Come then, come at me'' he said with his high pitched tone. 
 
 He put on his mask and leaped from laying an onslaught of offensive strikes. His opponent was clearly struggling trying deflect each and when he parried his friend's fencing sword to the side he charged his shoulder into his chest sending him on to the ground. He was lying and in a second was lifting himself up but too late the bulb was at his throat. 
 
 The man towering over him had won and removed his sword from his friend's throat and offered his hand out too him. 
 
 He accepted the towering friend's hand quickly he pulled him to his feet. He was looking up at him. The man had used his owned dirty tricks against him as such was karma. 
 
 His friend took of his mask and looked down into him. 
 
 `` You thought you had me there'' his cheeky smile was being flaunted in his face 
 
 `` I thought I did, it had to end it has been going on for an hour'' he removed his masked.
retelling:
Narrative Perspective: The Higher-Pitched Voiced Man (His Opponent)

In the heart of a sprawling estate, bathed in the golden light of twilight, I stood on the grand granite patio, my footsteps echoing off the winding stair pathways that encircled a hedge, leading into a lush meadow with willow trees, oak trees, and ash trees, a picturesque tableau framed by the window of a large room behind an engraved oak door. The air was thick with anticipation as I readied myself for my fencing duel against my aged-faced opponent, my heart pounding rhythmically beneath the weight of my masked visage.

I cast a sidelong glance towards the towering figures of lions, dragons, and knights etched into the door, their stone eyes seeming to watch over us with silent, approving nods. I knew that the fate of these ancient symbols was not in their hands but mine. The acoustics of the vast hallway amplified my opponent's voice as he charged at me, his sword clanging against my own in a steady rhythm of steel on steel.

With practiced grace, we danced around the marble floor of the large room, our duel punctuated by swift lunges and expert parries. My opponent, with his seasoned skill and furrowed brow, accused me of cheating when he found himself disarmed. I chuckled beneath my mask, for if there was one thing we both knew, it was that our rivalry transcended the boundaries of fair play.

"All is fair in love and war," I retorted, my voice ringing out across the room with an air of defiance. My opponent's eyes narrowed, but he did not falter in his attack. The duel continued, each blow landing with a resounding echo that seemed to shake the very walls of the estate.

In the end, it was I who emerged victorious, employing the same underhanded tactic that had caused my opponent such ire. As he stood before me, defeated and breathing heavily, I removed my mask, revealing my face to him for the first time in what felt like an eternity. His eyes widened in shock, but his gaze quickly softened as a friendly smile spread across his lips.

"You always were the better man," he said, extending a hand towards me. I accepted it, feeling a weight lift from my shoulders that I hadn't even realized was there. We stood there for a moment, our breaths mingling in the cool night air, before the narrator's voice broke through the silence, noting the hour that had passed without our notice.

Together, we stepped out onto the patio, the lions, dragons, and knights watching over us as we made our way into the meadow, our friendly rivalry forgotten for now in the gentle rustle of leaves and the soft call of a distant owl. The estate seemed to breathe a sigh of relief as the duel came to an end, and I knew that I had not only won a fencing match but also reaffirmed the bond between two old friends who would continue their dance for years to come.
